findings.finding: Exactly _Lower.returned_view_field, _Lower.expr and optional prepared arguments in _Lower.call change. Checker, Resource IR, Core verifier, Python Machine, LLVM backend and scalar export selection remain byte-identical to the parent.

Every recursive returned_view_field call rechecks a known non-extern function, matching read/mut return and borrow mode, one declared original borrowed formal, byte slice/Buffer type and scalar-only other value arguments. The terminal origin must remain one named byte place or ordinary owner-record field; stored local View and aggregate origins are rejected.

A freshly checked constructor-field path records returned_fields; an arbitrary value with a similar loan-list shape cannot enter the returned-call View path. The final chain requires one immediate parent, matching one-atom types, parent last loan equal to its capability, exact parent-prefix plus child, and no repeated capability names.

The recursive path loops over the original call.children once in source order. Only the declared origin recursively adapts; every other argument uses the unchanged expr path. The completed keys are passed to the existing call once, preventing duplicate scalar evaluation. Independent four-level short-circuit controls additionally exercised branch-generated CFG interfaces before and after every origin.

Existing call copies the parent loan stack and appends the actual returned child. Existing _State.prune follows borrow_parents transitively. new_block retains aliases under resource renaming; edge requires equal parent binding and alias relation. These unchanged functions carry all ancestors through branches, loops and early returns.

Existing reverse loan ending plus consume removes each ended capability from all aliases. Shared lexical aliases retain obligations until the final alias; mutable whole-local move transfers them, and explicit drop ends descendants before ancestors. Existing source/ResourceIR and Core verification reject missing mutable drops, live-owner release and inconsistent joins.

Owner evidence covers allocation refusal with normal return, stopped budget ledgers and exact ancestor corruption refusals. Native C observers verify successful-return allocation/free balance only. Traps, cancellation, foreign lifetimes, general unwind cleanup and RSS are not established by this increment.

The 36-capability selector set is exactly old349 plus new10; other35 capabilities and all top-level contract authority/boundary claims are unchanged. A former same-mode nested-call exclusion is deliberately replaced with a still-forbidden permission-change control. Existing single-call Core outputs retain their old identities. The default v1 route does not gain nested stored-return support.

The unchanged source byte limit, parser depth limit, specialization limits and primitive Core verifier remain gates. Python remains the production authority, Rust remains a finite comparison Machine, public LLVM exports remain scalar and optimization remains no_change. No broad strict blocker is closed.

The owner collector invokes the original unittest suite and records actual start/success/stop counts, all materialized source bytes/modes and tool hashes. Its bounded-compiler observer calls the original runner with unchanged arguments/options and returns the original completion or propagates its exception. It copies temporary IR/artifact bytes; it does not patch assertions or manufacture execution results.
